methods_only_design: Plants randomly assigned to supplemental hand-pollination versus open-pollinated control; treatment-specific relative-fitness selection gradients estimated on the same standardized floral traits; fruit herbivory measured but not experimentally manipulated.
classification_rule: One registered biotic modifier (pollination availability) is experimentally manipulated while consumer identity/composition is not manipulated.

methods_only_design: Open-pollinated and supplemental hand-pollinated plants are compared with treatment-specific phenotypic selection gradients; predispersal seed-predator damage is recorded naturally rather than manipulated.
classification_rule: One registered biotic modifier (pollination supplementation) is experimentally manipulated; antagonist pressure is observational.

methods_only_design: Across two study years, selection on floral traits is compared between open-pollinated and pollen-supplemented plants; florivore/herbivore damage is monitored at natural levels rather than experimentally manipulated.
classification_rule: The experimental manipulation changes one biotic modifier (pollen supplementation); antagonist damage remains a measured background process.

methods_only_design: Directional selection via seeds per plant is estimated under ambient conditions, reduced pollinator access, and reduced pollinator access combined with increased foliar herbivory.
classification_rule: The experimental context varies pollinator access and herbivory as two registered biotic dimensions.
